utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We don't have any interpretation, Mr. Djurdjic. We will have to find out what the problem is. I see I am being recorded, but perhaps you can speak --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Somebody has now come on air, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djordjevic, please look at tab 66 in your binder, the last two documents. We'd like to see document D007-2398, which is 304 according to the 65 ter list. Mr. Djordjevic, this is a decision on disciplinary proceedings from the 26th of May, 1999. Can you briefly tell us what this is about. What disciplinary proceedings were in question?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision which the chief of the SUP, in keeping with the decree on disciplinary proceedings, the war decree shall I say, after having established a breach of work duty instituted against the responsible staff member. In keeping with all the principles in the war decree in respect of breach of duty, disciplinary responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was the measure?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The measure was termination of -- termination of employment on the day the disciplinary proceedings were completed on the 26th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page number 4 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we see before us something in connection with the first document. Will you explain.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in parallel with the establishment of disciplinary accountability and the pronouncement of a measure against the responsible worker in disciplinary proceedings, the chief of the criminal investigation service of the secretariat in Pristina in respect of the same worker submitted to the district prosecutor a criminal charge, a criminal report, namely, against Dragan Kovacevic and Dragan Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having processed the information and obtained some additional intelligence, the district public prosecutor in Pristina was submitted in addition to the criminal report, the criminal charges, a special report which explained in detail. I provided proof for the criminal offence that the responsible staff member was charged with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the basic document --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please go slowly, Mr. Djordjevic, so that everybody will be able to follow, notably the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, because for the sake of the transcript, who submitted the separate report and the complaint to the prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents were submitted, were filed, by the authorised officials of the secretariat in Pristina, which is the secretariat which has territorial and subject matter jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any connection with these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the customary proceedings once the perpetration of a criminal offence has been established, and this is what we see before us. It is a record on the admission of a criminal complaint; namely, on the 20th of May, 1999, a citizen presented himself to the crime investigation department of the secretariat in Pristina and reported that someone of the police staff had committed a criminal offence in respect of him. After this first document, the crime investigation service then works to establish who the perpetrator of the crime was and finds -- writes up these documents and files them with the prosecutor's office for the latter to institute proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are lists of security-related incidents and events for the 18th of May submitted by the Pristina SUP to the staff, and it was later processed by the staff and forwarded to the ministry, addressed to the minister, to the chief of the public and state security sector, sent to the analysis administration. So this is a usual summary of events and occurrences of daily incidents which would be submitted to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please take it easy. Go slowly, Mr. Djordjevic. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have before me a document of the 19th of May, which is a summary of events and occurrences related to security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who is the author?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ministry's staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page number 3 of this page -- of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under item 3, in keeping with our discussion yesterday, the graver criminal offences committed, felonies committed, the staff MUP informs the ministry precisely of the criminal offences that have been committed by the policemen Dragan Markovic and Dragan Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor where that is exactly on this page.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in the Serbian version page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, which part of page 3?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the top, under the title 3, felonies committed, paragraph 1. So the Secretariat of the Interior from Pristina informed the staff about this crime, and the staff processed it as part of the daily occurrences report and forwarded it to the Ministry of the Interior, irrespective of the fact that the Pristina secretariat through regular forms of informing had already informed of this incident at the duty operations centre of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean the collection of documents? They will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D417.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document D007-2394. It is 303 according to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your number 67, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 7th of June, 1999, where under the chief of the secretariat in Belgrade meted out the measure of termination of employment to a worker in his secretariat who was responsible for grave breaches of work duty whilst he had been engaged as a member of the PJPs in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija. So this is the principle of the procedure whenever any breaches of work duty are established within the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D418, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we give the accused new hard copies of the documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see Exhibit P49. Can we have it brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this is a Law on the Ranks of Members of the Ministry of the Interior. Yesterday when we spoke about your career, you told us that this law had been passed in 1995 and that the titles were then translated into ranks. Can you tell us in brief how this law was applied in practice within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia passed this law, and by his decree the president of the republic promulgated that law. After that, in the Ministry of the Interior changes were made in the rules on the staffing scheme, the job description schedule, and the work posts were brought into accord with this legislation by introducing ranks instead of the previous titles, designations of posts. This law envisaged ranks corresponding to educational qualifications for secondary, post-secondary, and university education, in other words. Once the ranks were correlated with their work posts, there was a re-vamping and new appointments were made within the ministry with each staff member getting a relevant decision, each member of the force was eligible to be given a rank, to be confirmed a rank in keeping with this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now comment on Article 6 of this law.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all authorised officials, ranks were designated except for generals who in accordance with Article 6 would be conferred their ranks by the president of the republic; namely, the minister could not bring such a decision and decide who would be given the rank of general, but in compliance with this law the authority to do so was vested in the president of the republic. And the president of the republic by exercising his authority according to that article would promote authorised officials to the rank of general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a specific situation which concerns students, cadets, who have completed the police academy. Upon graduation, they would also be promoted by the president of the republic, i.e., he would be the one to confer upon them their official ranks, which I think was one of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see document D010-0382.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's your tab 69, and it's 65 ter 1464.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely the situation we discussed, the assignment of generals. By his decree, the president of the republic appointed generals to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia; and the personnel office issues letter of appointment specifying rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When was this published in the Official Gazette and which rank were you given by virtue of this decree?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 27 March 1996 was the date of its promulgation, and I received the rank of lieutenant-colonel [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the decree is dated 27 March, but when was it published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Official Gazette was number 53/95.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, at the top of the Official Gazette page you have the date.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 28 March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That means it was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia a day after it was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I please tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, by this decree the accused appears to be given the rank of lieutenant-general. The transcript suggests that he was given the rank of lieutenant-colonel. Do I take it that line 8, 8, should read "lieutenant-general," not "lieutenant-colonel"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. As usual, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us repeat. Which rank did you receive?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-general, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have this document admitted now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, D010-0382 will be Exhibit D420. And, Your Honours, correction for the record: The previous two documents, D007-2398, which was given D417, should be Exhibit D418. And D007-2394, which was given D418, should be Exhibit D419. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D010-0384 and the 65 ter is 1465.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your tab 70, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Official Gazette of the 10th of July, 1997, published the decree of the president of the Republic of Serbia, whereby he promotes generals within the Ministry of the Interior. And it was then that he promoted me into lieutenant-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's correct in B/C/S, but in e-court it's 28th March 1996. That's what we have on the screen. Perhaps there was an error when this was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're saying the correct date in Serbian as appears is the 10th of July --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian it's all correct, the 10th of July, but I believe the wrong translation was uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, the promotion of the accused is correct. He's promoted to the rank of colonel-general, and that's the day after he was appointed to the rank of lieutenant-general, according to the English translation, so rapid advancement. But we will accept for the moment, in the absence of anything else, that this actually occurred on the 10th of July, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a photocopy of the Official Gazette. Perhaps the accused can read out the dates and his proper rank into which he was promoted. Would that deal with the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, the date on the second page of the English translation shows the 6th of July, 1997. We -- I suggest, Mr. Djurdjic, you proceed on the basis that this occurred in July 1997 and there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll deal with that easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, tell us the number of the Official Gazette and the dates.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of the Official Gazette is 29, and the dates is 10 July 1997. That is when I was promoted from lieutenant-general into colonel-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document now be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit D421.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D008-6731, and the 65 ter number is 1425.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 71.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decree of the president of Serbia, whereby he promotes graduates of the police academy into second lieutenants of the police force, whereafter they are appointed to their work posts. This was done with every new generation of cadets, and that is how they received their first rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3 now -- or rather, page 4. One page back in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what about this letter of the 11th November 1998, what is it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of the interior presents to the president of the republic on the 11th of November, 1998, a draft decree and a list of graduates of the academy so that the president can issue a decree on their promotion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D422.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 4009, Prosecution's 65 ter list and the Defence 65 ter list is 1127.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who gave proposals with reasoning concerning promotions of generals?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the republic always received them from the Ministry of the Interior, and only on the basis of the minister's proposal could the president issue such decrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does this document show an example?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We need to see page 2. Yes, this is one such written proposal of the minister sent on the 11th of May, 1997 -- 1999, to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we tender this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D423.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D009-0789, and the 65 ter number is 1698.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 73. Before we move on to this document, could you tell us about the security and political situation in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija towards the end of 1997 and in the beginning of 1998.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security situation at that time was extremely complex because the separatist forces in Kosovo and Metohija wanted to attain their goals by use of arms, by armed force. And after certain events in Albania in 1997, a certain amount -- rather, a large amount of weaponry was smuggled into Kosovo and Metohija from Albania. These weapons were then distributed in end 1997 and early 1998, although there were certain terrorist attacks against the police before. But in end 1997 and early 1998 these attacks identified and resulted in many more deaths and injuries among the police. These attacks were mounted by extremist and terrorist forces. Ambushes were set for the police so that -- the security situation was extremely bad. The same terrorist forces were extremely active in punishing their own fellow citizens who recognised the Republic of Serbia or had official or business ties with the official authorities of Serbia. Kidnappings and disappearances of people were very frequent, both of ethnic Albanians and Serbs and members of other ethnic communities in the province. That was the main feature of the security situation. It was very complex and involved frequent use of fire-arms and heavier weapons even.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see a statement, a communique, of the Ministry of the Interior of the 5th March 1998. Were there any serious terrorist acts at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time in the Likosane and Cirez villages areas the police went on a regular mission in a Lada Niva vehicle, and on the section of the road between these two villages the police -- this police patrol was ambushed, on which occasion two members of the police were killed from that patrol and two of them sustained grievely [as interpreted] bodily injury. After that, all these units were engaged from the Secretariat of the Interior in Pristina as well as members of the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit from Pristina in order to rescue the injured policemen and to organise the pursuit of these terrorists. So the anti-terrorist unit from Pristina was also engaged in this action. In these - shall I say - show-downs with the terrorists, a number of terrorists lost their lives. All in all, in 1998, in January of that year, that was the most serious incident and terrorist attack, which attack took place in territory where the -- where there was a terrorist group operating headed by Jashari. So in the year before this group had executed a number of terrorist attacks and killed a number of policemen in the area covered by the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, i.e., in the Drenica area. This was the most drastic example of terrorist attack and the one with the gravest consequences to both the police and to the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djordjevic, thank you. But repeat for the transcript, please, after the attack in Likosane on the police patrol what happened?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that attack units of the Secretariat of the Interior of Pristina were engaged. So a part of their special units, the "posebne" units, and a part of the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit from Pristina, with the objective of rescuing the injured members of the police and for pursuit of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there any victims among the policemen, and were there any victims -- casualties among the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have already said that on that occasion four policemen lost their lives, that was in the terrorist attack itself, and also while they responded to it there were a number of injured policemen, wounded policemen as well. And later a number of terrorists lost their lives in these clashes. And I've said that that was the most serious incident at the beginning of that year with grave consequences, both to the members of the police and to the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now tell us something about the information that the MUP had on the activities of the group of Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public and the State Security Services had extensive intelligence and evidence of perpetrated terrorist attacks by this group for a year or two back. They had precise information in terms of in which particular terrorist actions this group had participated and what the consequences had been affecting members of the police or citizens that were also targeted by these attacks. In other words, they had very good knowledge of all the criminal activities of this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did this group participate also in the terrorist attack in the village of Likosane?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, members of this group were precisely those who laid the ambush and who liquidated the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What measures did the ministry undertake in connection with the activities of Adem Jashari's group?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, in the year before against this group, as well as against other members of terrorist groups which were operating in the area of Kosovo, the Ministry of the Interior would file criminal complaints attaching all the evidence that they had at their disposal against these terrorists. This was one line of activity, and this was the regular criminal procedure line. The other thing proceeding from such a complex situation and the consequences of terrorist activities, the minister of the interior ordered a co-ordinated action of the public and State Security Services to deprive of liberty members of this terrorist group, including Jashari. To that end, the minister set up a special staff for this particular mission only and designated its members under the minister's decision. The leader of the staff was the chief of the public -- of the state security department, at that time Jovica Stanisic, and I was his deputy as at that time the chief of the public security department, with members of the staff being from both the public and state security departments. This staff drew up a plan for the arrest, the deprivation of liberty, of members of this terrorist group. That plan was compiled. We had operative intelligence on the location of the terrorist group, and preparations commenced in order to implement and practice the plan to deprive of liberty this group. In the course of these preparations and while members of the police were getting nearer the areas where the terrorists were, an attack was also launched against these police members; and that is when the realisation of the entire plan started on the basis of the available data also that this group was retreating towards buildings, facilities, in which Jashari resided.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was in charge of the operational preparation of the plan?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In drawing up this plan, participated both members of the state security and the public security departments because it basically contained the obligation for members of the public security department to cordon off the broader area of future action and thus prevent any lateral attacks, outside attacks, on the engaged policemen, whilst practically the actual deprivation of liberty in the buildings where Adem Jashari was there in that area was to be carried out in keeping with a plan with a unit of the state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was a report filed on this action that had been carried out?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the action had been completed, the head of the staff - and on this occasion I have to underline only that the head of the staff was Jovica Stanisic, but at that particular point in time he was sick so that standing in for him was Dragisa Ristivojevic, his deputy. So Dragisa Ristivojevic as the one in charge of the operations to realise the plan informed the minister of everything, and the minister informed about the action and its consequences the Government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, prior to the beginning of this action were any measures taken?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The plan itself envisaged, regardless of the fact that this was an extremely dangerous terrorist group and also that they had information that there was also a number of -- there were also a number of civilians in the area, so civilians were called by a public address system, through a public address system, to leave the territory where the terrorist group was in order to avoid any consequences, lest the civilians come to any harm. So that a large number of civilians, the majority of the civilians, who were in the area complied with that warning, and it was made possible for them to move away from the broader area, from the cordoned off area where the members of the police were. And they left the area where activities to deprive this group of liberty would later take place. According to subsequent information, a number of civilians were forbidden by Adem Jashari to leave the area. He used them as a human shield, as a defensive shield, against a possible attack from -- against a possible attack from the police. And in this action against the terrorists, regrettably some civilians also came to harm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, did this group headed by Adem Jashari put up an armed resistance to the police?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the warning that had been given and after a group of civilians had pulled out, this activity further unfolded with the use of fire-arms by the members of the police who were engaged in the action after Adem Jashari with his group had opened fire from different weapons that he had available at that particular location, targeting members of the police who wanted to deprive of liberty that group of terrorists. There were machine-guns, sub-machine-guns, and other heavier weaponry that was used in offering armed resistance to the police, whose task was to deprive this group of their freedom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you tell us whether judicial organs, after the completion of this action, had implemented the procedure envisaged under the law?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the completion of this action, when the resistance of the terrorists was crushed and their armed resistance to the police ceased, the competent judicial organs carried out an on-site investigation. And according to the order of the judicial organs, their bodies were taken to the forensic service for a proper processing officially; and the judicial organs were fully involved and discharged all their regular obligations after the terrorist attack, or rather, after this clamp-down -- crack-down on the terrorists. And also, some journalists' organisations or some diplomatic representatives who at the time were in Kosovo and Metohija visited the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what happened with the staff that you have been talking about after the completion of the action?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This staff was set up for that particular terrorist action, anti-terrorist action, only. We saw the composition of the staff which I had set up which was functioning in Pristina at that time, and we concluded that in terms of its personnel that staff had not been equipped and capable of responding, taking up these most important challenges; so that appreciating that fact the minister set up this ad hoc staff. After the completion of the action and the filing of the report, this staff ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, who was responsible for the work of this staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leader, the head of the staff, was the one who was responsible for the work and operation of this staff and that was the head -- chief of the state security sector -- department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who -- to whom was he answerable for his work?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have before us this communique of the Ministry of the Interior. Which service was this from, do you know, this statement?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the minister's office there was a service, an information service, that served the minister. And as they were in charge of public relations and liaised with the media, they drew up this statement and submitted it to the media, to television station studios, and to the written media.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here we see names of persons who were both deprived of liberty after the action as well as those who were let go after the action. Who was in charge of doing that particular segment of the work, this particular -- these particular operative measures after the action?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operative measures were taken by both members of the public and state security departments after the actions in terms of establishing the specific criminal liability of the persons who were deprived of liberty on that occasion and the -- it was the public security department that established their degree of criminal responsibility, normally also using information of the state security department. This was their regular work. It was to be established whether there were any elements of criminal conduct in their actions and whether it required further procedure in terms of filing the case with the prosecutor's office and other organs or whether they should be set free.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D424.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 706. P706.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, here we see a dispatch of the 22nd of April, 1998. Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic is the person who signed. Can you comment?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from end April 1998. The Ministry of the Interior had made an evaluation of the security situation. This situation was assessed as very serious. That is why certain preparations were made for the units who were supposed to be engaged to be prepared; and for that purpose the chief of the public security sector sent to all secretariats and the MUP staff in Pristina a letter ordering that lists be updated, first of all; second, pursuant to the order of the minister mentioned in paragraph 1, he ordered that the entire reserve police force be summoned and inspected. It was also ordered that preparations be made for training and a training course organised for reserve police officers. All these steps needed to be taken so that members of the police be prepared for the most complex tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To whom was this sent?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all secretariats in the area of the Republic of Serbia and the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get P709.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we see a dispatch of 29 April 1998 signed by you. What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was aware of the complex security situation in Kosovo. Everyone was aware that a large number of extremists and terrorists in -- terrorists in Kosovo were armed and prepared to put up resistance, and it was to be expected that the police would also mount certain actions to neutralise them. There were certain groups who wanted to take advantage of these -- of this grave security situation and the unrests in order to commit crimes, and there were groups who were even prepared to go to Kosovo specifically to take advantage of the general situation to commit crimes. And in this letter I say that these categories of perpetrators should be focused on and that their incursions into Kosovo should be prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge, in 1998 or 1999 in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija were there any paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me take 1998 first. There was not a single paramilitary unit or unit of volunteers, nor were there any individuals volunteers who took part in any activities mounted by the police or the army. The entire complement of the police force and of the army were professionals and reservists who had been prepared and trained. At that time we paid great attention to this problem to prevent the arrival of any groups who would be bent on crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any volunteer unit or paramilitary unit that was engaged. Everything was being done in keeping with the current legislation as far as the police and the army are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P705.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we see here a dispatch signed by you. The date is 29 April, 1998. To whom was this sent and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for the ministry to keep the situation in this territory under control, it had the duty to prevent the entry of undesirable persons and to prevent also the smuggling of weapons or other material intended for terrorist activity. In this context this is an instruction to the secretariats close to the border with Kosovo and Metohija, instructing them to install check-points, to inspect both passengers and vehicles, to prevent the smuggling of fire-arms and other undesirable materials or persons wishing to enter Kosovo. All these secretariats are outside of Kosovo except for Pec, and this dispatch was sent from the secretariat of Pec. And these measures were ordered because the secretariat of Pec is on the border with Montenegro, and there are travel routes from Montenegro that penetrate directly into the territory of Kosovo, namely, an area covered by the secretariat in Pec. That's why only this secretariat was told to put up two check-points on routes that lead from Montenegro into the territory of Pec, and we knew from earlier intelligence that there is a lot of smuggling of weapons and drugs and large movements of people along these routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P708.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, the date on this dispatch is 30th April. You sent it. Can you tell us to whom and what is the topic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a customary dispatch sent to all secretariats and organisational units of the Ministry of the Interior. It was normally sent ahead of state holidays. In this case it is the 1st of May, labour day, and ahead of all holidays the police stepped-up its presence and measures on the ground to prevent any terrorist acts, to enforce law and order in places where large numbers of citizens would gather. And this was a very peculiar time in Kosovo, and we were expecting some terrorist activities to spread from Kosovo to the territory of Serbia. This dispatch indicates that the police measures were intensified. In addition to the usual measures on holidays, a special duty service was ordered everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document D010-0322.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we see a dispatch dated 10 June from the minister of the interior to the president of the republic, Mr. Milan Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see that it was also sent -- we see that a dispatch from an inter-sector staff is attached, inter-departmental staff. Can you tell us about this staff and the situation prevailing in Kosovo and Metohija at the time.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security situation continued to become more and more complicated, illegal import of weapons from Albania continued, and a new form of terrorist activity appeared, namely, the blocking of roads, important thoroughfares in Kosovo and Metohija. At this time, sometime in May, the road from Pec to Djakovica via Decani was blocked. At that time the regular police used this road and turned off towards a village near Streoc on a regular assignment, when a terrorist attack happened killing the commander of the police station in Pec. The police helped -- other police officers helped this unit that was on mission. The whole unit was pulled out, including the assistant commander who was killed. And on that occasion the terrorists cut off the Pec-Decani road, and the road could no longer be used by anyone. That was a very important road; it still is. It's not far from the border with Albania, and that was the territory through which arms were smuggled. That road was completely cut off for a number of days. There was no traffic. The minister created an inter-departmental staff, appointing the chief of state security as head of the staff - at that time that was Jovica Stanisic, I was his deputy - and this inter-departmental staff also included leaders of various public security sections. The main task of this staff was to provide for unhindered traffic, open all roads. The blockade lasted for several days. The terrorists had fortified the territory they were holding, and we had to neutralise those fortifications and enable traffic to resume. And after several days, this road, Pec-Djakovica-Decani, was again opened. The task of the staff and the way we went about it is we worked only to re-open that road and to neutralise the points, the features, from which the terrorists were controlling the road, stopping, disabling, traffic. In order to ensure that unhindered traffic would continue, we put up certain check-points to prevent further attacks. There were a number of incidents - and we heard testimonies here. On that road Pec-Djakovica -- or rather, Pec-Decani-Djakovica, the village of Prilep lies. And in all these activities in 1998, 1999, this village was badly affected. When we freed one section of this road, we came practically halfway into this village and we put up a check-point there. Our only goal was to prevent terrorists from blocking roads in the future and stopping their incursions. In 1999 -- in 1998 and 1999, nine policemen and many -- were killed and many more were wounded in various attacks, but we did not mount any major operations against terrorists on that occasion. Our only -- our main task was to re-open the road. We chose the most favourable locations on the road to put up our check-points, to prevent further roadblocks. We did not -- we managed to do that with the main road; however, the terrorist forces were very strong in that area and they continued to block byroads within the territory they controlled, because all these villages were almost exclusively Albanian. At that time the municipality of Decani where all this was going on had a population of 70.000, including only 700 Serbs and Montenegrins. All the others were ethnic Albanians, and the terrorist organisation was very present in this area. At that time we had certain intelligence, that the situation is deteriorating, that armed smuggling is going on, and the inter-departmental staff sent this dispatch to the minister, highlighting the security situation, and giving its assessment of possible future developments. As we see, the minister made this brief available to the president; and after our action to deblock the road, following the minister's instruction, we, or rather, the head of our staff reported to the president to inform him what we had done and for that meeting -- ahead of that meeting the minister sent this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You referred to Prilep and you said that it had been frequently mentioned here. Tell me, according to what you know, were there any terrorist activities undertaken targeting Prilep whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This village was right in the middle of this arterial road which passed through it. They primarily attacked the police check-points while we were there, and they inflicted major injury on us affecting mostly the policemen who came to harm while they were discharging their duties at the check-points. Of course those terrorist attacks were responded to. There were frequent exchanges of fire, but the movements of the units were not towards the area where the terrorists were. They were only engaged to repel attacks, to prevent them from re-taking the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know what resources, what means were used by the KLA members in such attacks?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they used automatic rifles, conditionally speaking light infantry weapons; very often they resorted to sniping, sniper fire was used; as very often they also used recoilless guns and anti-tank resource and armaments. Because we were holding that check-point with armoured vehicles so they would attack us with mortars, with recoilless guns, with hand-launched throwers, with heavier-calibre weaponry and with high destructive power.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was responsible for the work of this staff that was set up to unblock the Djakovica-Pec road?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the staff was Jovica Stanisic, the chief of the state security department, and he was responsible for the work of the staff and for the implementation of the planned tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who informed the minister about the work of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the staff did. This is an example of him as the chief of the state security department sending a dispatch to his own deputy, Dragisa Ristivojevic, who was to forward it to the minister. And normally there was regular informing from the ground by telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D425.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, can you tell us what happened with this staff after the Pec-Djakovica road was unblocked?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, namely, the head of the staff and I myself, at a meeting with President Milutinovic attended by the head and the members of the staff, we pointed out to certain problems, saying that it was difficult to deal with the very grave security challenges and that the security situation was deteriorating. And we suggested that there should be another way which should be adopted in order to organise these complex tasks and duties. Let me just revert to the existence of the previous staff which I had set up a year before. After the 10th of June, the personnel was to be replaced of this staff, namely, the chief of the staff and the members of the staff because their mandates, their terms, in the staff of a year had expired. Giving some thought to the possible future leader of the staff, mindful of the overall security situation, it was my opinion that we should opt for a very experienced person, both in terms of positions of leadership as well as experience with Kosovo and security in general. So I proposed General -- Major-General Sreten Lukic to be appointed to the post of chief of this staff, who at that time was the assistant municipal secretary for the uniformed police. I proposed this some ten days before the staff was to be set up because the replacement time was drawing near. He agreed with my proposal because I told him that this was a man who had completed the military academy, had been to Kosovo on a number of occasions, had participated in complex activities, and had the necessary experience in directing and managing units. So I proposed to the minister to put him on the operations staff because he had not been to Kosovo for some time before that so that he would learn the ropes, as it were. So he was with us for a while in our staff, and after this meeting was held at President Milutinovic's office, in view of the fact that the decisions were to be issued to replace the chief and members of the staff, on the 15th of June with approval from the minister I drew up the decision that we have already discussed and by it I appointed Lukic as head of the MUP staff. Those were personnel reinforcements in view of the situation that obtained. After these talks in Milutinovic's office and after we all perceived that we should differently organise the entire MUP structure in order to be able to act in the forthcoming difficult security circumstances, the minister decided to change the concept of the ministry staff. This he did by bringing together through the staff both services with all their capacities in terms of police units, namely, from the public security department, as well as in terms of organisational units, namely, the secretariats and centres of the state security department in Kosovo and Metohija. That was the situation which the minister bore in mind when he chose to set up and structure this staff in this way, and practically thereby to revoke my previous decisions and form this ministry staff in this way. This inter-departmental staff that we have been referring to ceased to exist after the road had been deblocked and the relevant report sent, and that was the end of that staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P76 -- P760, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is your decision designating the members of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'd like to see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what was the date of this decision, this personnel decision that you brought?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 11th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the decision that you referred to just a while ago?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that, the minister brought this decision, this other decision, that you have talked about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Several days later and after having assessed on his part what the situation was like and also based on our proposals, the minister decided to set up the staff, as he did set up later, by this decision of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall now like to go back to Prilep for a while and the clearing of this road. Please tell me, how was this planned, how was it planned, what resources, what assets would be used to combat the KLA in order to achieve that unblocking of the road?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that the fortifications that the terrorists had erected on the salient elevations around the road were fortified very well indeed, and that practically without heavier assets that we had available we would not have been in a position to deal with their fortifications, i.e., to crush their resistance. In that sense, during the action there was extremely selective use targeting only a few critical points of army assets, namely, resources that the police did not have available, and not having which it could not deal with the fortifications and other structures actually hindering traffic on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, can you tell us how were the civilians treated whilst this action, this -- these anti -- while anti-terrorist actions in this period were being mounted?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the execution of all actions that were mounted at that time, the activities of all forces targeted terrorists exclusively. Strict care was taken not to -- for the civilians not to sustain any casualties during clashes with terrorists, and whenever there was the possibility certain specific actions would be adjusted precisely in order to avoid civilians coming to any harm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, for the sake of the transcript, when Mr. Djordjevic -- when Mr. Lukic became a member of this staff for the unblocking of the road, where had he previously worked, in what organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant head of the Secretariat of the Interior of the city of Belgrade, and he was as such assistant secretary. He was responsible for the uniformed segment of the police force there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see Exhibit D234.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is your number 79.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a dispatch which the minister of the interior sent on the 18th of June, 1998, to all organisational units of the ministry, practically both to the public security department and to the state security department and MUP staff in Pristina as well as to all internal organisational unit in the public security department and the state security department, to the centres of the state security department, to the secretariats, the public security secretariats, all of them, and to the heads of the internal organisational units at the headquarters of the ministry. It -- the dispatch is actually an instruction, and it concerns the treatment of and conduct of both public security department and state security department representatives vis-a-vis members of the diplomatic and consular obligations and representatives of all other international humanitarian and other organisations in Serbia and in the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, how did the security situation unfold thereafter, in midyear, in June? Can you explain.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only saw the further aggravation of the security situation. There were more pronounced actions by the terrorists, intensified actions by the terrorists, which could be seen left, right, and centre. And at that time they carried out all their major tasks which they had planned. It was at that time that they actually carried them out. As I've already mentioned, they blocked -- they had previously blocked the less important roads, but later this was not satisfactory for them. They also started to block the main roads, the arterial thoroughfares in Kosovo. Then their activities also targeted important industrial facilities, which they're of significance both to Kosovo and to Serbia as a whole. Namely, they carried out their most complex and most dangerous actions at that time. Their role was completely exposed at that time, namely, it was their desire to achieve by arms what their objective was. They wanted to attain their earlier political objectives in this way in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were referring to some main roads that had been blocked. What was this about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principal artery leading from Pristina to Pec was blocked by barricades erected at several points, the major one being from the direction of Pristina near the village of Lapusnik and from the direction of Pec it was just outside Klina, somewhere around Dolac. They took advantage of the exceptionally favourable ground features there. They erected very sound fortifications, dug trenches along those roads. They also installed barricades, barriers, and other obstacles, and practically in that way blocked the main road leading from Pristina to Pec. Also taking advantage of the favourable geographical conditions, they blocked in the same way the road leading from Pristina via Stimlje to Pristina. The road which led to Mitrovica was the one in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija that was not blocked, and another one from Urosevac to Macedonia and via Mitrovica to Montenegro as well. Although, all these roads most often the one towards Mitrovica they launched terrorist actions. But as a rule, in contrast to the roads which I referred to previously, these roads were serviceable. These were the most important roads. There were also some other regional roads where traffic was not possible. This primarily refers to the regional Kosovska Mitrovica-Pec road via Klina and Istok. There they erected barricades near Istok, and thereby prevented traffic from unfolding all together on that road. In this way, according to our assessment, over 50 per cent of the territory was conditionally speaking under the control of the KLA. Namely, public traffic was impossible in that area as was the movement of all citizens in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did such actions have repercussions on the economic life of the province and of all the citizens, the functioning of political activities as well?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These actions of course impacted on the entire life of the province. Of course, the economy could not function properly because traffic on the main roads was disabled so that if you want to go -- if you wanted to go from Pec to Pristina you had to take a round-about road, a much worse one; to reach Prizren you had to cross mountains. And since the movement of citizens was made impossible, discontent was great among the ethnic Albanians but even more among non-Albanians who were affected. They were all concerned and feared for their safety, and of course they had no freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there any attacks that resulted in the capture of vital economic installations?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such things happened as well. One of their actions targeted the open-pit mine and thermal power-station Obilic. The terrorists first intercepted a bus carrying workers to their shift and kidnapped ten of them. Then they put up roadblocks and blocked the track along which ore was brought to the power-station, and the power-station could not work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P707.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 80. This is a dispatch signed Vlastimir Djordjevic. The date is 1st of July, 1998. What is it about and what measures are proposed here?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was sent from the public security sector on the 1st of July, 1998, and it was sent to the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija and secretariats close to the border with Kosovo, Vranje, Leskovac, Prokuplje, Kraljevo, and Novi Pazar. These secretariats border on the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija. It was also sent to all the posts of the border police in Kosovo and various organisational units in the headquarters of the ministry. The dispatch describes the security situation in the province, saying that it is deteriorating and becoming even more complex, and then certain measures are proposed to the secretariats on the border, behind the border, to prevent illegal import of weapons and other materiel, as well as measures of co-operation with and among state authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we go on, there's just a comment that was incorporated into the question that the witness just answered. It says: "This is a dispatch signed by Vlastimir Djordjevic." I wonder if that's correct or if the witness could explain if he signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, who signed this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign it myself. I think it was signed on my authority by General Obrad Stevanovic, but this is a typical example of how tasks were given by the minister. I must have been away on that day, so I did not sign myself. But the situation was reviewed, and the minister instructed that such a dispatch should be sent to units on the ground, and under my name this dispatch was indeed sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see D106, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We are looking at a decision by the minister dated 19 July 1998. Can you describe to us the subject of this decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first say that the usual document on the staffing scheme, it is stipulated that all members of the police force received an increased credit while they were serving in such conditions, and it was a system of points. They received ten more points for service in those circumstances; and this decision says that when these members are engaged in special assignments such as suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija, the minister decided that for each day of engagement members of special units of the police - that is PJPs, the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit, and the unit for special operations of the state security - should receive 50 dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able as chief of the public security sector to issue such a decision to reward members of the unit for special operations?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. This could be done only by the minister, and finally the minister also decided on all financial matters so that even in my own public security sector I could not make such a decision. It was up to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see D008-6724. The 65 ter number for the Defence is 1429.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And your tab 82, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of citizens who were killed in the course of terrorist actions --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Prosecution it's -- the 65 ter number is 1424.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a list of citizens killed in the terrorist actions perpetrated by Albanian separatists in Kosovo and Metohija between the 1st of January and 8th July 1998. This list was prepared by the analytics administration of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see a summary here with a total.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first part of this report lists individually the citizens who were killed by the terrorists, indicating their ethnicity and their personal details as well as the locations where they were liquidated. And in the summary at the end we see the total number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. For the record, could you tell us again which service and for whom prepared this report.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The analytics service of the Ministry of the Interior for the minister, for the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D426.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, it's pointed out to me that the document is headed "Ministry of Foreign Affairs" in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me see. It's a mistake. It's a mistake in the translation. It should be "Internal Affairs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now see document D008-6662, and the 65 ter number is 1421.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your tab 83, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list we saw a moment ago is a list of people who were killed by the terrorists, and the list we see now includes civilians abducted by Albanian terrorists between the 1st of January and 7th of July, 1998. They are listed individually indicating ethnicity, Serbs, Montenegrins, Albanians, and others. It also includes members of the Ministry of the Interior who were abducted because a number of our own members were kidnapped at the time, and on page 13 of this paper there is a summary, just a list of numbers, where we see that a total of 105 persons were abducted at the time of this report and their fate was unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see here also who was released and who was killed, but it says that 56 persons have not been heard from since. Did you ever find out what happened to these people, there were 56 of them at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think any of them were found alive. I'm not quite sure, but I -- I'm pretty sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I move to tender this document now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D427.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we are now in the month of July 1998. Could you tell us how the situation evolved after that meeting at Milutinovic's office, after the decision was passed to establish the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now we were discussing the terrorist action when the thermal power-station was stopped from working. That operation finished when the terrorists were pushed away from that area. A hundred officers were providing security for the thermal power-station from that moment on, and later on the power-station built up its own security detail. But the overall situation required that roads be deblocked and operations be launched to neutralise the terrorists and arrest them. To that end the highest political leadership passed the requisite decisions and a plan of anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija was drawn up, and in the period that followed that plan was complemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you find out about that plan?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our activities up to that moment we had contacts with President Milutinovic concerning all of our activities, and sometime towards the end of July, the minister said that on Milutinovic's orders we were to go to see the President of Yugoslavia, Slobodan Milosevic, to discuss the situation in Kosovo and Metohija. Therefore, since the topic was designated, the minister decided to invite to that meeting both the chief of the public security sector and the chief of the state security sector, as well as the head of the staff of the ministry in Pristina, Sreten Lukic; as well as Assistant Minister, Obrad Stevanovic, who was responsible for the uniformed part of the service. So that is the group in which we went to see President Milosevic. Also present were the top military leaders, the Chief of General Staff, the chief of military security, and the commander of the Pristina Corps, as well as the commander of the 3rd Army under which the Pristina Corps served. There was the president of Serbia and several other politicians at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who informed you of the agenda?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Milosevic opened the meeting and informed us that the Supreme Defence Council had met a few days previously, making a decision to draw up a plan to fight terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. On that occasion he informed us that the army was in charge of drawing up that plan, that is to say the Yugoslav Army, and he informed -- actually, the commander of the Pristina Corps, General Pavkovic, informed all the presidents about the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In what way was this plan presented to you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This plan was presented to us orally, and it contained several stages, as stated by General Pavkovic. The army and the police forces and the expected areas of operation to neutralise and fight terrorist units was shown to us on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever have this plan in writing in your hands?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw both in the map and in the texts that this plan included practically all the units that the ministry had available, including the PJP. The map showed the locations, but we were really surprised that none of us present there had been involved in drawing up this plan. Practically by being presented with the obligations that our forces had really took us by surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you ever had the written version of this plan and the map, you personally?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, neither me personally nor any part of the ministry or the public security department had an opportunity to review the plan, either in general nor the map that showed the deployment. After the meeting, the plan and the map were taken away and practically we never had any contact with that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, can you please repeat whether you ever had an opportunity to see the written version of the plan and the map that was relevant to that.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never had an opportunity to review the plan, nor the map that was presented at the meeting. I also know that other members of the ministry who attended the meeting did not have an opportunity, either then or later, to review the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which ministry are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You just told us that this plan -- actually, tell us what units were envisaged to be used according to this plan?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan envisaged the use of army units of the Pristina Corps that were deployed down there as well as PJPs, a Special Anti-Terrorist Unit of the public security department and the unit for special operations of the state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the methodology of use of these units according to what General Pavkovic told you at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed us on the map the locations, the approximate locations, of deployment for each unit in the territory, and based on the plan, decisions were made later where and in what way each unit was going to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there any mention at the meeting who was to direct the units participating in the operations in general?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no mention at all at the meeting about who was going to be in charge of this operation. Later, the plan was adopted in the form that it had been presented. The president said that the documents relating to the implementation of this plan was -- were to be drawn up by the Yugoslav Army and that according to these plans the Ministry of the Interior units were going to operate as well as the units of the Yugoslav Army. There were no personal indications as to who was going to command the units. It only contained the tasks for both the state organs, indicating how they should act according to the plan in fighting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there any mention of the designation of the commander of all the units participating in these activities?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was never mentioned. There was no personnel decisions relating to the command function. These organs were given the task to accomplish the main tasks of the plan, which was to fight terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But in what way were they supposed to accomplish this task?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that in order for us to be able to implement this master plan, it was necessary pursuant to our respective obligations to prepare separate plans for each activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. We are talking about this meeting, so tell us only this: At this meeting was there any discussion, either generally or specifically, about the implementation of the plan?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the state organs were given the task and it was up to the state organs to implement the plan through co-ordinated activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on what you told us, what else was discussed at the meeting, or was that the end?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the main topic. I don't think there was any significant discussion. There were no contentious issues. The plan as such was, so to say, adopted in a way, and we proceeded with the implementation accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting with the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting the minister of the interior called a meeting attended by Sreten Lukic, Obrad Stevanovic, and myself. The minister, in accordance with the already-assigned mission to the Ministry of the Interior, wanted to have it implemented and to ensure that the Ministry of the Interior could be up to the task and carry out the plan. At that moment, it was indisputable that the staff - as he put it and as it had been set up - would continue to work with Sreten Lukic at the helm. And having in mind the importance of the forthcoming task, the importance for the state, he instructed us to be there, meaning General Stevanovic as a police official and myself, to be there during the execution of this task of fighting terrorism so that the ministry and we personally could fulfil our obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned General Lukic and what his task was. As for you and General Obradovic what --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Obrad Stevanovic. Can you tell us what you too were expected to do in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time there was no task more important for the state but for the ministry as well. Significant police forces were engaged -- or rather, that was the plan, to engage significant forces for this task.
